title: ISO/IEC 22123-3:2023 — Cloud Computing Reference Architecture (CCRA) — Scope
text:
ISO/IEC 22123-3:2023 Scope

This document specifies the Cloud Computing Reference Architecture (CCRA). The CCRA provides a vendor-neutral reference architecture for cloud computing. It describes cloud computing in two complementary views:

1. User view (Clause 8): describes cloud computing in terms of roles, sub-roles, activities and the relationships between parties involved in cloud computing (CSC, CSP, CSN).

2. Functional view (Clause 9): describes cloud computing in terms of functional components organised in a layered framework (user layer, access layer, service layer, resource layer, multi-layer functions).

Clause 10 describes the relationship between the user view and the functional view.

The CCRA enables a common understanding of cloud computing for vendors, service providers and customers, and supports cloud standards development, procurement decisions and compliance assessments.

title: CCRA user view — CSC role and sub-roles
text:
Cloud service customer (CSC) role — user view (Clause 8.1.1–8.1.2)

The CSC role is played by a party that uses cloud services for their business goals. CSC sub-roles and activities:

8.1.2.1 CSC:cloud service user: Uses cloud services to accomplish tasks. Activities include: use cloud service (provision credentials, invoke cloud service, receive outcomes); perform service trial (trial cloud services for business fit assessment).

8.1.2.2 CSC:cloud service administrator: Administration and management of cloud services and their use. Activities include:
- Monitor service: Track usage, monitor integration with ICT systems, define measurement points and performance indicators, monitor SLA compliance, evaluate data transfer regulatory compliance.
- Administer service security: Ensure appropriate security for CSC data; implement backup/recovery plans; administer security policies; define encryption and integrity technologies; handle PII in CSC data.
- Handle problem reports: Assess problem impact, troubleshoot, open problem reports with CSP, develop workarounds, escalate problems.
- Administer tenancies: Configure user accounts, security roles, identities and permissions; identify and control shared data; create/remove tenants; define enforcement policies.
- Connect ICT systems to cloud services: Integrate existing ICT components with cloud services; map business data; provision access rights; define security requirements including confidentiality and integrity of data flows; integrate logging and security incident management.

8.1.2.3 CSC:cloud service business manager: Business aspects of using cloud services. Activities:
- Perform business administration: Manage accounting, financial management, billing.
- Select and purchase service: Examine CSP offerings, negotiate terms, accept contract.
- Request audit report: Request cloud service audit report for compliance purposes.
- Provide billing and usage reports: Prepare reports of cloud service usage and billing.

title: CCRA user view — CSP role and sub-roles
text:
Cloud service provider (CSP) role — user view (Clause 8.1.3)

The CSP role includes activities that make cloud services available, ensuring delivery to the CSC and service maintenance. CSP sub-roles:

8.1.3.2 CSP:cloud service operations manager: Responsible for all operational processes ensuring services and infrastructure meet operational targets. Activities: prepare systems, monitor and administer services, manage assets and inventory, provide audit data.

8.1.3.3 CSP:cloud service deployment manager: Plans deployment of services into production. Defines operational environment, initial deployment steps and dependencies, and operations processes. Activities: define environment and processes, define and gather metrics, define deployment steps.

8.1.3.4 CSP:cloud service manager: Ensures CSP's services are available and function correctly per SLA; also ensures smooth operation of business and operational support systems. Activities: provide services, deploy and provision services, perform service level management.

8.1.3.5 CSP:cloud service business manager: Overall responsibility for business aspects of offering cloud services to CSCs. Creates and tracks business plans, defines service offering strategy, manages CSC relationships. Activities: manage business plan, manage customer relationships, manage financial processing.

8.1.3.6 CSP:customer support and care representative: Main interface with CSC, reacting to customer issues and queries. Activity: handle customer requests (support, reports, incidents from CSCs).

8.1.3.7 CSP:primary inter-cloud provider: Relies on secondary CSPs to provide part or all cloud services to CSCs. Main activities: intermediation, aggregation, arbitrage of secondary CSP services. Activities: manage cloud services from secondary inter-cloud providers, perform intermediation/aggregation/arbitrage.

8.1.3.8 CSP:cloud service security and risk manager: Ensures appropriate management of risks associated with development, delivery, use and support of cloud services. Ensures information security policies of CSC and CSP are aligned. Activities: manage security and risks, design and implement service continuity, address regulatory compliance obligations.

8.1.3.9 CSP:network provider: Provides network connectivity and network services to CSC, CSN and other CSPs. Activities: provide network connectivity, deliver network services, provide network management services.

title: CCRA user view — CSN role and sub-roles
text:
Cloud service partner (CSN) role — user view (Clause 8.1.4)

The CSN role encompasses activities that support or are auxiliary to the CSP role or CSC role, or both.

8.1.4.2 CSN:cloud service developer: Responsible for designing, developing, testing and maintaining cloud service implementations. Can involve composing service implementations from existing services. Activities:
- Design, create and maintain service components: Design software components, create functionality, process problem reports, provide fixes and enhancements.
- Compose services: Create service functionality by composing existing services; design interface to CSC representing composed services.
- Test services: Test components and services ensuring complete and correct functionality; test interoperability with secondary CSP cloud services.

8.1.4.3 CSN:cloud auditor: Conducts audits of provision and use of cloud services. Audit typically covers operations, performance and security. Evaluates whether specified audit criteria are met (e.g. ISO/IEC 27002 for security). Evidence from CSP in procedural document or log record form. Activities:
- Perform audit: Request/obtain audit evidence, conduct tests, obtain evidence programmatically, redact sensitive information, compare evidence against audit criteria.
- Report audit results: Provide documented report of audit results.

8.1.4.4 CSN:cloud service broker: Negotiates relationships between CSCs and CSPs. Not itself a CSP. Acts only during the contracting phase. Activities:
- Acquire and assess customers: Provide information to potential customers about services and SLAs; negotiate terms and prices; assess customer needs.
- Assess marketplace: Survey CSP product offerings; subscribe to change notifications; match offerings to customer needs including technical, business and regulatory aspects.
- Set up legal agreement: Negotiate service agreement between CSC and chosen CSP(s).

title: Cloud computing activities
text:
Cloud computing activities (Clause 8.2)

8.2.1 A cloud computing activity is a specified pursuit or set of tasks delivering one or more outcomes. Activities are categorised into three main groups: activities that use cloud services (CSC role), activities that provide cloud services (CSP role), and activities that support cloud services (CSN role).

8.2.2 Activities associated with the CSC role:
- Use cloud service: Using CSP services to accomplish tasks.
- Perform service trial: Using cloud services on trial basis to assess business fit.
- Monitor service: Track service quality against SLA; monitor usage, integration, performance indicators; evaluate data transfer regulatory compliance.
- Administer service security: Ensure data security; implement backup/recovery; administer security policies; define encryption; handle PII.
- Handle problem reports: Assess impact, troubleshoot, open reports with CSP, escalate issues.
- Provide billing and usage reports: Prepare reports for CSC:business manager.
- Administer tenancies: Configure user accounts, security roles, identities, permissions; create/remove tenants; define enforcement policies.
- Perform business administration: Manage accounting, financial management; track billing.
- Select and purchase service: Examine CSP offerings; negotiate; accept contract.
- Request audit report: Request report from cloud auditor or CSP.
- Connect ICT systems to cloud services: Integrate ICT components with cloud services; map business data; provision access rights; define security requirements; integrate logging and security incident management.

8.2.3 Key activities associated with the CSP role:
- Prepare systems: Assess impact of new deployments; modify/expand data centre resources.
- Monitor and administer services: Monitor services and infrastructure; capture significant events; administer network infrastructure, storage, user/system privileges; maintain operating systems and hypervisors.
- Manage assets and inventory: Track all compute, storage, network and software assets including versions, patch levels and configuration; manage on-boarding of new assets and secure disposal.
- Provide audit data: Collect and provision data relevant to audit requests; create and send audit information from logs; redact sensitive information or PII.
- Define environment and processes: Define technical environment (compute, storage, network resources, software dependencies); define scaling policies; assure cloud service conforms to standards; define processes for running service.
- Provide services: Accept and process service invocations; manage service fault handling; maintain service and infrastructure; automate system processes; manage capacity and performance trends.
- Deploy and provision services: Make service implementations available at network endpoints; follow deployment processes.
- Perform service level management: Monitor metrics against SLA targets; take action when metrics do not meet SLA values; report problems.
- Manage security and risks: Define information security policy; assess risks; implement security controls (identity/access management, data protection, infrastructure security, incident management, governance, physical/personnel security, network security, multi-tenant isolation).
- Design and implement service continuity: Consider potential failure modes; implement recovery processes for availability within SLA terms using failover and redundancy.
- Ensure compliance: Implement regulatory compliance and standards conformance.
- Provide network connectivity: Set up network connections including VPN and dedicated bandwidth connections with appropriate bounded delay, jitter, bandwidth and QoS.

8.2.4 Key activities associated with the CSN role:
- Design, create and maintain service components; compose services; test services; perform audits; report audit results; acquire and assess customers; assess marketplace; set up legal agreements.

title: Cross-cutting aspects in the CCRA
text:
Cross-cutting aspects in the CCRA (Clause 8.3)

Cross-cutting aspects apply to multiple elements within the CCRA and are shared issues across roles, activities and functional components. For the CCRA, cross-cutting aspects are as described in ISO/IEC 22123-2, Clause 7.

8.3.2 Auditability: Assurance that cloud services are provided and used in consistency with associated service agreements between CSCs, CSPs and CSNs. Most often achieved through independent audits. Audit depends upon data and evidence relating to usage, environment, availability and performance of services — including records and logs maintained securely.

8.3.3 Governance: Each role implements governance according to its needs. Cloud governance is cited as cross-cutting because of the requirement for transparency and the need to rationalise governance practices with SLAs and contractual elements of the CSC-to-CSP relationship.

8.3.4 Interoperability: CSC should be able to use widely available ICT facilities in-house when interacting with cloud services, avoiding proprietary or specialised software. Also covers ability for one cloud service to work with other cloud services (through inter-cloud relationships or multi-cloud composition). Standards implement interoperability between components or support portability of data and program components.

8.3.5 Maintenance and versioning: Governance of service and resource maintenance is critical. Maintenance practices should be documented in the SLA. Versioning of services (and components) is important so customers know which version is in use. Where significant changes are made between versions, the older version should remain available for an agreed period.

8.3.7 Portability: Cloud data portability allows CSCs to copy CSC data into or out of a cloud service by network access or physical transfer. Cloud application portability allows migration of fully-stopped VMs or machine images (IaaS) or application components (PaaS). CSPs should adopt standard data interchange formats.

8.3.8 Protection of PII: CSPs should protect the assured, proper and consistent collection, processing, communication, use and disposition of PII. Cloud provides flexible solution for shared resources but also poses confidentiality challenges.

8.3.9 Reversibility: The right-to-be-forgotten principle applies — when CSC indicates intention to cease use, there should be an orderly process for CSC to retrieve data and for CSP to delete all copies after an agreed period.

8.3.10 Security: Security spans all views of the reference model from physical security to application security. Security is a shared responsibility — CSPs and CSCs collaboratively design, build, deploy and operate cloud computing systems. Security capabilities include: access control, confidentiality, integrity, availability, early detection/diagnosis/fixing of problems, secure logging, firewalling, malicious attack detection and prevention. Distribution of security responsibilities depends on service category (IaaS: more CSC responsibility for app security; SaaS: more CSP responsibility).

8.3.11 Service levels and SLAs: The cloud SLA characterises quality of cloud services delivered in terms of measurable properties (business and technical) and cloud computing roles. CSC needs a cloud SLA specifying technical performance requirements, security, and remedies for failures. The SLA should define data classifications (CSC data, CSP data, derived data), who has access and control, and how data can be used.

title: CCRA functional view — layering framework
text:
CCRA functional architecture — layering framework (Clause 9.1)

The functional architecture describes cloud computing in terms of high-level functional components. Functional components represent sets of functions required to perform cloud computing activities for various roles and sub-roles.

The CCRA uses a layering framework with four layers plus multi-layer functions:

9.1.2.2 User layer: The user interface through which a CSC role interacts with a CSP role and with cloud services, performs customer administrative activities, and monitors cloud services. Represents all functions required for the interface between a CSU (CSC:cloud service user) and any available cloud service.

9.1.2.3 Access layer: Provides a common interface for both manual and automated access to the capabilities available in the services layer. Responsible for: presenting cloud service capabilities over access mechanisms (web pages, web services); applying security functionality (authentication, authorisation of users, credential validation); handling encryption and request integrity; enforcing QoS policies on traffic from/to the user layer.

9.1.2.4 Service layer: Contains the implementation of the services provided by a CSP; contains and controls software components that implement the services, and arranges to offer them to users via the access layer. Service implementation software relies on the resource layer capabilities to meet SLA requirements.

9.1.2.5 Resource layer: Includes equipment typically used in a data centre (servers, network switches, routers, storage devices) and non-cloud-specific software (host OS, hypervisors, device drivers, systems management software). Includes the cloud transport network functionality providing underlying connectivity between CSP and CSC(s) and within the CSP and among peer CSPs.

9.1.2.6 Multi-layer functions: Span all four layers; include:
- Operational support systems (OSS): runtime administration, monitoring, provisioning, maintenance
- Business support systems (BSS): product catalogue, billing, financial management
- Security systems: authentication, authorisation, auditing, validation, encryption
- Integration capabilities: linkage of different components to achieve required functionality
- Development support capabilities: creation, testing and lifecycle management of services

title: CCRA functional components — user and access layer
text:
CCRA functional components — user layer and access layer (Clause 9.2.2–9.2.3)

User layer functional components:
- User function: Supports the CSC:cloud service user to access and use cloud services. Can be as simple as a browser or as sophisticated as an enterprise system running business processes, applications, middleware and infrastructure.
- Business function: Supports CSC:business manager activities — selection and purchase of cloud services, accounting and financial management. Business capabilities are offered via cloud services.
- Administration function: Supports CSC:cloud service administrator activities — administration of user identities and profiles, monitoring service activity and usage, event handling and problem reporting. Cloud administration capabilities only accessed using cloud services.

Access layer functional components:
- Access control: Limits users to use of particular services. Involves authentication of users through validation of credentials, followed by authorisation to use specific services; includes identity management. Should be provided for cloud services, their dependent resources, and related control functions.
  - Service access: Provides access to cloud services offered by the CSP.
  - Business access: Provides access to business capabilities offered by the CSP.
  - Administration access: Provides access to administration capabilities (operations support systems).
  - Development access: Provides access to capabilities supporting development, test and maintenance of cloud service implementations.
- Connection management: Enforcement of QoS policies on traffic from/to user layer functional components.

title: CCRA functional components — service and resource layer
text:
CCRA functional components — service layer and resource layer (Clause 9.2.4–9.2.5)

Service layer functional components:
- Service capabilities: Consists of the necessary software to implement the service offered to CSCs; implements the functionality defined by the service interface (the interface offered to CSCs, independent of the service implementation).
- Business capabilities: Provides capabilities for accessing the business function related to provision of cloud services; the business function is contained within business support systems functional components.
- Administration capabilities: Provides capabilities for accessing the administration function related to provision of cloud services; contained within operations support and business support systems.
- Service orchestration: Provides coordination, aggregation and composition of multiple service components in order to deliver the cloud service. Specifies required cloud resources and the dependencies between the resources.

Resource layer functional components:
- Resource abstraction and control: Used by CSPs to provide access to physical computing resources through software abstraction. Enables efficient, secure and reliable usage of underlying infrastructure. The control feature enables management of resource abstraction features. Can include software elements such as hypervisors, virtual machines, virtual data storage and time-sharing. Enables capabilities such as rapid elasticity, resource pooling and on-demand self-service.
- Physical resources: Represent the elements needed by the CSP to run and manage cloud services. Include: computers (CPU, memory), networks (routers, firewalls, switches, network links), storage components (hard disks). Resources inside data centres (computing servers, storage servers, intra-data centre networks) and those outside data centres (inter-data centre networks, core transport networks).

title: CCRA functional components — multi-layer functions
text:
CCRA functional components — multi-layer functions (Clause 9.2.6)

9.2.6.1 Integration functional components: Connect functional components to create a unified architecture; provide message routing and exchange mechanisms; include:
- Security integration: Provides integration to security capabilities including authentication, authorisation, encryption, integrity verification and policy mechanisms.
- Monitoring integration: Provides connection from access, service and resource layer functional components to monitoring and reporting capabilities of OSS.
- Service integration: Provides connections to services in the provider's environment; virtualises services so location and implementation details are hidden from dependent components.
- Peer service integration: Connects to services of peer CSPs with appropriate security and accounting for usage, linking to CSC identity.

9.2.6.2 Security systems functional components: Apply security-related controls to mitigate security threats; encompass all security facilities required to support cloud services:
- Authentication and identity management: Capabilities for user identities and credentials to authenticate users when accessing cloud services; supports federated identity management for single sign-on across multiple cloud services.
- Authorisation and security policy management: Control and application of authorisation for users; definition and application of security policies relating to cloud services.
- Encryption management: Capabilities for encryption of data at rest or in motion; encryption key management and scheme selection.

9.2.6.3 Operational support systems (OSS) functional components: Set of operational management capabilities required to manage and control cloud services:
- Service catalogue: Listing of all cloud services, all relevant technical information required to deploy, provision and run a cloud service.
- Provisioning: Capabilities for provisioning service implementations and access endpoints; manages cloud resource requirements and quotas.
- Monitoring and reporting: Monitors cloud computing activities of other functional components; provides reports (alerts for time-sensitive behaviour, aggregated historical data); stores and retrieves monitoring/event data as logging records. Must guarantee availability, confidentiality and integrity of logging records; multi-tenant isolation of log data.
- Service policy management: Defines, stores and retrieves policies (business, technical, security, privacy, certification) applying to cloud services.
- Service automation: Capabilities for service delivery including execution of service templates and orchestration; holds service templates defining cloud computing activities and workflows for provisioning.
- Service level management: Manages capacity and performance relating to a cloud service against SLA requirements; tracks overall state of allocated and available resources; identifies bottlenecks; supports capacity planning.
- Incident and problem management: Captures incident or problem reports; manages through resolution. Reports from CSP systems or CSCs.
- Platform and virtualization management: Manages underlying CSP resources (compute, storage, networking) and virtualisation (hypervisors). Resources organised into resource pools with standardised hardware, automated workload shifting, protection and isolation of workloads.
- Peer service management: Connects provider's OSS and BSS to administration and business capabilities of peer CSPs; establishes communication paths; passes appropriate identity and credentials.

9.2.6.4 Business support systems (BSS) functional components:
- Product catalogue: Lists all cloud services of a CSP with technical information for deployment and provisioning; serves as service entry for cloud products.
- Account management: Manages CSC relationships including contracts, subscriptions, entitlements, service pricing and policies for treatment of CSC data. Subject to stringent availability and security requirements.
- Subscription management: Handles CSC subscriptions to particular cloud services; records new or changed subscription information.
- Metering and billing: Metering (measurement of consumption), rating (application of pricing schedules), invoice generation and transmission; cost accounting and apportionment.
- Accounts: General ledger and accounting functions including accounts receivable and payable for the CSP organisation.

9.2.6.5 Development support functional components:
- Developer environment: Supports development of service implementation software; connects to CSP environment resources, integration with other services and security capabilities; supports creation of configuration metadata and deployment scripts.
- Build management: Supports building a ready-to-deploy software package including service implementation software and configuration metadata.
- Test management: Supports execution of test cases against service implementation builds; produces test reports. Testing performed in a specialised test environment closely approximating production.

title: Relationship between user view and functional view
text:
Relationship between the user view and the functional view (Clause 10)

10.1 This clause describes the logical relationships between the roles, cloud computing activities and functional components in the CCRA. Standards associated with a relationship can specify degrees of information flow or other types of interoperability, and ensure specified degrees of quality (e.g. security or service level).

10.2.1 Service capabilities functional component: The cloud service is offered via a service interface and can offer one or more cloud capabilities types under the service capabilities functional component. For SaaS or CaaS cloud service categories, the service capabilities functional component contains the application-specific software or communication applications deployed onto the resource layer so that SLA service levels are achieved.

10.2.2 Common roles, activities and functional components: The CSP:cloud service manager (8.1.3.4) performs the provide services activity (8.2.3.8), providing the cloud service for CSC:cloud service users to actually use. Before use, the service must be developed and deployed. Two CSN sub-roles are involved: CSN:cloud service developer develops the implementation using developer tools; CSN:cloud auditor performs audit activities and reports results. After deployment, CSC:cloud service administrator performs administer tenancies activity using the administration function functional component to set up the tenancy and grant access rights to CSC:cloud service users.

10.2.3 Multi-tenancy and isolation: A tenant is a group of CSC:cloud service users sharing access to a set of physical and virtual resources. Multi-tenancy is the allocation of physical or virtual resources such that multiple tenants and their computations and data are isolated from and inaccessible to one another. Multi-tenancy affects both cloud services themselves and the business and administration capabilities. Log records, subscriptions, usage and billing information are kept isolated and visible only to customers who own the related tenancies.

title: CCRA — Further details on user view and functional view relationships
text:
Annex A (informative) — Further details regarding the user view and functional view

A.1 CSC – CSP relationship: Three key elements:
1. CSC:cloud service user using provider cloud services to achieve business goals.
2. CSC:business manager using CSP business capabilities to subscribe to and manage cloud services.
3. CSC:cloud service administrator using CSP administration capabilities to administer the use of cloud services.

A.1.1 Functional relationship: CSC:cloud service user performs the use cloud service activity through the user function functional component → invokes cloud service through service access functional component → performs authentication and authorisation → if authorised, invokes service capabilities functional component which performs the request using resource layer functional components.

A.1.2 Business relationship: CSC:cloud service business manager performs activities (select and purchase service, perform business administration, request audit report) through the business function functional component. Business function invokes business capabilities of CSP through business access functional component. Business capabilities interact with BSS functional components: product catalogue, account management, subscription management.

A.1.3 Administration relationship: CSC:cloud service administrator performs activities (monitor service, provide billing and usage reports, administer tenancies, administer service security, handle problem reports) through the administration function functional component. Administration function invokes administration capabilities of CSP through administration access functional component. Administration capabilities interact with OSS: monitoring and reporting.

A.2 Provider – peer provider (inter-cloud) relationship: Primary CSP takes the CSC role with secondary CSPs. Services of the secondary CSP are offered to and used by customers of the primary CSP. Three interfaces: administration interface, business interface and service interface. Key considerations: security, protection of PII, data ownership. Primary provider must ensure SLA offered by secondary provider's services meets requirements of primary provider's services.
